title: Navier × Grab
subtitle: SEA water-mobility — ridehail integrated across 19 cities
executive_summary: Grab is Navier's single highest-leverage growth opportunity in SEA. The super-app already owns last-mile demand across 19 markets where surface water-mobility is undersupplied, congested, or simply missing. Navier brings the asset — hydrofoiling electric and hybrid vessels with a 2,000 nm range envelope on Quanta-LR — and the network operating model. A regional partnership across SEA converts Grab's existing demand into water-mode revenue and positions Navier across the fastest-emerging archipelagic mobility region globally.

narrative.headline: Singapore — SEA Quanta-LR Hub
narrative.body: Pilot anchor. Singapore is the regional Quanta-LR hub: MPA-friendly waters, certification-credible flag, 11 berthing/charging POIs already mapped (Marina Bay → Sentosa → Jurong → Tuas). Phase 1 launches Pioneer II inter-island commutes (Marina Bay ↔ Sentosa, ~3 nm; Marina Bay ↔ Lazarus, ~5 nm) inside the GrabRide product. Phase 2 stands up the Singapore-radial Quanta-LR fan to Batam, Bintan, Tioman, Desaru — all sub-300 nm, all already routed in our spine.

narrative.headline: Bali — Pioneer II tourist commute + Nusa entry point
narrative.body: Pilot 2. Benoa ↔ Nusa Penida/Lembongan is the dominant water-taxi corridor today; current fleet is slow, wet, weather-exposed. Pioneer II runs the route at 30 kts in foil, dry cabin, 12 pax. Grab integration adds a hotel-pickup → boat-transfer → island-resort booking in a single super-app flow. Hospitality cluster (Bvlgari, Aman, COMO, Six Senses) is the upsell layer for higher-yield charter inventory.

narrative.headline: Bangkok — Chao Phraya commute + Pattaya entry point
narrative.body: Pilot 3. Chao Phraya river-line congestion is one of SEA's worst urban commute problems. Pioneer II foils above the chop quietly with no wake — a regulator-friendly story. Quanta-LR extends to Pattaya (~85 nm, Pioneer II edge / Quanta-LR comfortable) and Koh Samet. Competitor presence (Candela) = market-validation; Navier wins on Quanta-LR range and software.

narrative.headline: Phuket / Phang Nga — Andaman cluster
narrative.body: Steady-state. Phuket marina hubs anchor a Quanta-LR fan into Phang Nga Bay, Phi Phi, Krabi, and onward to Langkawi (cross-border, ~70 nm). Hospitality cluster: Aman, Soneva, Banyan Tree. Grab is already deeply embedded in Phuket inbound tourism flow — boat-mode integrates into existing airport→resort flows.

narrative.headline: Koh Samui / Phangan / Tao — Gulf triangle
narrative.body: Steady-state. Inter-island hop triangle: all sub-30 nm legs, Pioneer II ideal. Replaces existing ferry pain (long, slow, weather-dependent). Hospitality: Six Senses, Anantara, Banyan Tree all on-island.

narrative.headline: Langkawi — Andaman cross-border
narrative.body: Steady-state. Langkawi ↔ Phuket cross-border Quanta-LR entry point unlocks a previously-impossible direct route (currently ferry + bus + flight). Cross-border ridehail + immigration coordination via Grab's existing MY/TH operating relationships.

narrative.headline: Philippines — archipelagic Quanta-LR play
narrative.body: Steady-state. PH is the largest unsolved archipelagic mobility market in SEA. Manila → Boracay, Cebu → Bohol, Palawan inter-island. Grab Philippines is the #1 super-app — boat-mode is a structural addition to their inventory.

narrative.headline: Jakarta — Pulau Seribu + IKN adjacency
narrative.body: Steady-state. Pulau Seribu (Thousand Islands) Pioneer II fan from Ancol. Strategic: Jakarta is the ID base for the IKN Nusantara new-capital relocation — first global instance of new-capital greenfield mobility adjacency.

narrative.headline: Riau Islands — Singapore cross-border
narrative.body: Steady-state. Batam, Bintan, Karimun all sub-50 nm from Singapore — Pioneer II routes today. Anambas/Natuna are Quanta-LR entry points (sister-quad architecture). Cross-border ridehail SGP↔ID is the Grab Singapore + Grab Indonesia integration moment.

narrative.headline: Lombok — Mandalika DPSP
narrative.body: Steady-state. Mandalika is one of Indonesia's 5 priority super-priority destinations (DPSP). Quanta-LR refuel-mid-node at Lembar. Connects Bali ↔ Lombok ↔ Gili Islands ↔ Komodo on a single network.

narrative.headline: Komodo / Flores — Labuan Bajo DPSP
narrative.body: Steady-state. Second of the 5 DPSP destinations. Labuan Bajo is the gateway; Komodo NP boats today are slow and crowded. Pioneer II for in-park hops; Quanta-LR for Bali↔Labuan Bajo (~250 nm) which currently requires a flight.

narrative.headline: Raja Ampat — premium liveaboard entry point
narrative.body: Steady-state. Top-tier dive destination; current access is multi-hour open-skiff transfer. Quanta-LR entry point premium-positioned with Aqua Expeditions and the resort cluster.

narrative.headline: Wakatobi — Quanta-LR refuel-mid-node
narrative.body: Steady-state. Wakatobi resort + diving cluster; refuel-mid-node in our spine. Quanta-LR connects to Komodo and onward.

narrative.headline: Derawan / Berau — Kalimantan dive cluster
narrative.body: Steady-state. Refuel-mid-node. Sangalaki/Kakaban manta + jellyfish lake premium entry point.

narrative.headline: Banda / Maluku — spice-route heritage cluster
narrative.body: Steady-state. Quanta-LR-only market — historic spice route geography; Banda Neira heritage tourism, no current fast-ferry option.

narrative.headline: Lake Toba — inland DPSP
narrative.body: Steady-state. Inland-lake market (only inland market in the Grab/Navier overlap). DPSP destination. Pioneer II all-electric is uniquely suited to a clean inland lake.

narrative.headline: Vietnam — Halong, Da Nang, Phu Quoc
narrative.body: Steady-state. Halong Bay tourism entry point; Da Nang ↔ Hoi An coastal commute; Phu Quoc island-hopping. Grab Vietnam is dominant.

narrative.headline: Malaysia — Penang + Tioman + east coast
narrative.body: Steady-state. Penang island commute, Tioman ↔ Mersing (~55 nm corrected), east-coast hospitality. Grab MY base.

narrative.headline: Cambodia — Sihanoukville + Koh Rong + Taj
narrative.body: Steady-state. Sihanoukville ↔ Koh Rong / Koh Rong Samloem Pioneer II. Cambodia is a natural luxury-hospitality entry point anchored by a leading global hotel group.

partner_view.value_prop: Grab already owns last-mile demand across Southeast Asia's coastal and island cities, where surface water transfers are slow, fragmented, or unavailable. Adding quiet, fast, low-wake hydrofoil vessels to the Grab app turns congested harbours and inter-island gaps into bookable, premium water routes — a new high-margin mobility mode on demand Grab already commands.
partner_view.call_to_action: Scope a 3-city water-mobility pilot (Singapore, Bali, Bangkok) integrated into the Grab app.

title: Navier × Careem
subtitle: MENA water-mobility — super-app integrated across the GCC
executive_summary: Careem is the MENA mirror of the Grab opportunity in SEA — an established regional super-app covering 10 cities across the GCC and Red Sea where Navier has filled or stub city files. The opportunity: convert existing super-app demand into water-mode revenue across intra-city (Pioneer II) and intra-GCC cross-border (Quanta-LR) corridors. A Careem partnership is regulator-light versus public-transit deals — making it the fastest MENA path to landed revenue and a parallel de-risk for the government-channel work. Careem is now part of Uber, so a Careem regional partnership simultaneously opens a global Uber conversation.

narrative.headline: Dubai — anchor city, first boat in 2 weeks
narrative.body: Anchor and time-sensitive. First boat arrives in ~2 weeks; Careem is the fastest path to revenue while RTA is . CareemRide water-mode launches on Marina ↔ Bluewaters ↔ Palm ↔ Mina Rashid as a premium product. 14 berthing POIs already mapped at real OSM coords.

narrative.headline: Doha — Lusail + Katara + The Pearl
narrative.body: Pilot 2. Doha intra-city: Lusail Marina ↔ The Pearl ↔ Katara ↔ Banana Island. All <30 nm — Pioneer II. Katara is the Qatar hospitality/culture cluster. Cross-border Quanta-LR: Dubai ↔ Doha (~200 nm) as a same-day GCC business connector — currently a flight + transit.

narrative.headline: Manama — Amwaj + Reef Island + Dammam cross-border
narrative.body: Pilot 3. Manama intra-city + Bahrain ↔ Eastern Province KSA (Dammam, ~30 nm) cross-border — Pioneer II edge / Quanta-LR comfortable. Replaces the King Fahd Causeway congestion for premium time-sensitive travel.

narrative.headline: Abu Dhabi — Saadiyat + Yas + Western Region
narrative.body: Steady-state. Careem AD operations integrate with Saadiyat cultural cluster, Yas leisure, and Western Region Anantara entry point (Sir Bani Yas Quanta-LR).

narrative.headline: Sharjah — Khor Fakkan east-coast crossover
narrative.body: Steady-state. Sharjah's east-coast enclave (Khor Fakkan) on the Gulf of Oman is a Quanta-LR refuel-mid-node for the Musandam (Khasab) cross-border entry point.

narrative.headline: Ras Al Khaimah — Hayat/Marjan + Musandam cross-border
narrative.body: Steady-state. RAK ↔ Khasab (Oman exclave, ~25 nm cross-border) is a Pioneer II entry point — currently a 90-min drive across a border. UAE-flag precedent on this corridor is an open confirm item.

narrative.headline: Fujairah — east-coast Gulf of Oman
narrative.body: Steady-state. Fujairah ↔ Khor Fakkan ↔ Dibba intra-city Pioneer II + onward to Musandam Quanta-LR.

narrative.headline: Muscat — Bandar Jissah + Six Senses Zighy Bay
narrative.body: Steady-state. Muscat ↔ Bandar Jissah ↔ Daymaniyat Islands Pioneer II. Six Senses Zighy Bay (Musandam) is a premium hospitality anchor reachable via Quanta-LR from Dubai/RAK.

narrative.headline: Jeddah — Red Sea gateway + RSG adjacency
narrative.body: Steady-state. Jeddah is the operational gateway for Red Sea Global; Careem KSA is the demand layer for both Jeddah waterfront and RSG transfer logistics.

narrative.headline: Sharm El Sheikh — Red Sea South + RSG cross-border adjacency
narrative.body: Steady-state. Sinai resort cluster; near Red Sea Global on opposite shore. Cross-border Quanta-LR entry point into Saudi Red Sea coast as RSG matures.

partner_view.value_prop: Across the GCC, Careem's super-app demand maps directly onto underused waterways — Dubai Creek, the Marina, Doha Bay, the Red Sea coast. Hydrofoil vessels let Careem extend its mobility network onto the water with a quiet, zero-wake, premium ride that complements its existing ground fleet and opens cross-emirate water corridors.
partner_view.call_to_action: Define a GCC water-mobility pilot pairing intra-city electric routes with longer hybrid corridors.

title: Navier × UAE Waterfront
subtitle: Quiet electric foiling across Dubai & Abu Dhabi — transit, hospitality, cross-emirate
partner_org_canonical_name: UAE Transport Authorities (Dubai RTA + Abu Dhabi ITC)

headline_metrics.label: Emirates in scope
headline_metrics.sub: two markets, one Quanta-LR hop apart

headline_metrics.label: Hospitality entry point
headline_metrics.sub: Palm, Saadiyat, Yas, Sir Bani Yas

headline_metrics.label: Local-build path
headline_metrics.sub: regional production hub candidate at scale

executive_summary: The UAE is Navier's first and most time-sensitive MENA market — the first vessel arrives within weeks. Two complementary openings sit one Quanta-LR hop apart. In Dubai, the Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) operates the existing abra and water-taxi network — the natural public-transit partner for a quiet, wakeless, all-electric Pioneer II upgrade plus a Marina ↔ Bluewaters ↔ Palm ↔ Mina Rashid premium connector. In Abu Dhabi, the Integrated Transport Centre (ITC) pairs with a deeper hospitality opening across Saadiyat, Yas, and the Sir Bani Yas island resorts, and stands as the strongest first regional production-hub candidate as the local market scales. Pioneer II covers every intra-city leg; Quanta-LR stitches the emirates together and reaches Sir Bani Yas, Khasab, Doha and Manama as long-range premium connectors. Engagement across both authorities is coordinated locally; private-operator outreach runs in parallel as the near-term revenue path.

narrative.headline: Dubai — abra corridor electrification + premium Marina connector
narrative.body: Anchor city. 14 berthing POIs already mapped at real OSM coords: Dubai Marina Mall, Bluewaters, Palm Jumeirah, Mina Rashid, Dubai Creek + the abra stations on both sides of the Creek + waterside hospitality (Atlantis, Burj Al Arab, Madinat Jumeirah). Pioneer II is uniquely fit: <70 nm, all-electric, quiet-mode in harbor, 30 kts foiling above chop. The RTA proposal is a 12-month pilot on one premium corridor (Marina ↔ Mina Rashid) plus one heritage corridor (Creek abra augmentation), with conversion option to full -pilot. Quanta-LR uplift unlocks Dubai ↔ Khasab (cross-border, UAE-flag precedent ), Dubai ↔ Sir Bani Yas, Dubai ↔ Doha as long-range premium connectors.

narrative.headline: Abu Dhabi — Saadiyat + Yas intra-city + Sir Bani Yas long-range
narrative.body: Anchor city. Intra-cluster: Saadiyat marina, Yas Marina, Eastern Mangroves, Zaya Nurai. All <30 nm legs — Pioneer II all-electric. Hospitality cluster: Anantara (Eastern Mangroves + Sir Bani Yas + Qasr Al Sarab), Four Seasons, Edition, Rosewood. The Sir Bani Yas Anantara jetty is in our manual coord overrides — strategic premium entry point. Quanta-LR unlocks Sir Bani Yas as a same-day round-trip from AD city (~150 nm one-way, ~3.5 hrs each way at 30 kts foiling — vs. current 2.5 hr drive + 30 min boat). Production-hub conversion: at ~50 boats AD shipyard becomes the regional MRO + light-build base.

partner_view.value_prop: The UAE's iconic but ageing waterborne networks and its island geography are an ideal fit for hydrofoil electric vessels. In Dubai, the same abra and water-taxi corridors run quietly, wakelessly and with zero direct emissions, extending transit to the Marina, Creek and new districts. In Abu Dhabi, fast low-noise transfers link Saadiyat, Yas and the Western Region island resorts with a premium arrival experience. Quanta-LR then connects the two emirates and the wider Gulf on a single long-range platform — lifting throughput while cutting noise, wake and emissions.
partner_view.call_to_action: Trial an all-electric, zero-wake vessel on a live UAE corridor and map an inter-emirate connector.

title: Navier × Red Sea Global
subtitle: Greenfield hospitality cluster — Ocean Race 2027 as time-bound trigger

headline_metrics.label: Resort islands
headline_metrics.sub: Sheybarah, Ummahat, Coastal Village, multi-resort cluster

executive_summary: Red Sea Global is the single largest hospitality cluster opportunity in the global pipeline — a $50B+ greenfield development on the Saudi Red Sea coast with 16+ resort islands and zero existing surface-marine operator. The combination is unique: greenfield (no incumbent to displace), premium pricing power (ultra-luxury hospitality customer set), and a hard time-bound trigger in the Ocean Race Grand Finale 2027, which will put global attention on RSG waters and call for a visible, distinctive premium marine fleet. Quanta-LR commercial timing (H2 2026+) aligns with Ocean Race 2027 — the boats are ready, the showcase is built-in. Greenfield charging infrastructure means it can be specified from scratch; Quanta-LR removes the dependency entirely with refuel-anywhere range plus quiet electric operation in harbour.

narrative.headline: Red Sea Global — 16+ islands, greenfield premium fleet
narrative.body: Anchor cluster. Sheybarah, Ummahat, Coastal Village, and the broader 16+ island resort programme. All POIs are in our manual coord overrides (OSM doesn't index greenfield development). Pioneer II covers intra-cluster (all <70 nm). Quanta-LR (H2 2026+) unlocks RSG ↔ Jeddah (~250 nm) and RSG ↔ NEOM Sindalah (~180 nm) as same-day premium connectors. The model: an RSG-owned premium fleet scaled to the resort opening cadence, with the Ocean Race Grand Finale 2027 as the public showcase moment.

narrative.headline: Jeddah — operational gateway + Quanta-LR refuel-mid-node
narrative.body: Operational base. Jeddah is the air gateway for RSG inbound guests and a Quanta-LR refuel-mid-node on the Jeddah ↔ RSG (~250 nm) corridor. Jeddah waterfront also stands alone as a hospitality + Careem demand market.

narrative.headline: NEOM Sindalah — adjacent greenfield mega-cluster
narrative.body: Adjacent. NEOM Sindalah opens 2024–2025 with a yacht-club + 80+ berth marina and adjacent luxury resorts. RSG ↔ Sindalah (~180 nm) is a Quanta-LR corridor; the two clusters can be sold as a single integrated KSA Red Sea premium marine network.

partner_view.value_prop: A greenfield luxury archipelago needs a guest-transfer mode as refined as the resorts. Hydrofoil vessels deliver silent, zero-wake, zero-direct-emission island hopping that protects the marine environment the destination is built around — and provides a signature arrival experience with no legacy operator to displace. The infrastructure can be designed in from day one.
partner_view.call_to_action: Co-design the guest island-transfer network ahead of resort openings.

title: Navier × Singapore MPA
subtitle: Maritime and Port Authority — certification-credible flag and SEA Quanta-LR hub
partner_org_canonical_name: Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore
executive_summary: Singapore Maritime and Port Authority (MPA) is the de-facto regulatory home base for SEA water-mobility and the most certification-credible flag in the region. The MPA story is a regulatory de-risk play that simultaneously unlocks (a) Singapore as the SEA Quanta-LR commercial hub, (b) the Singapore-radial cross-border Quanta-LR fan into Indonesia and Malaysia, and (c) certification credibility that accelerates every other SEA market including the Grab regional partnership. MPA is the lead agency; LTA supports intra-city commute integration. Singapore's progressive maritime regulator stance (electric harbour-craft mandates, autonomous-vessel sandboxing) makes it a willing first mover.

narrative.headline: Singapore — SEA Quanta-LR Hub
narrative.body: Anchor city. 11 berthing/charging POIs mapped: Marina Bay, Sentosa, Lazarus, Jurong, Tuas. MPA pilot scope: (1) Pioneer II inter-island commute (Marina Bay ↔ Sentosa, ~3 nm; Marina Bay ↔ Lazarus, ~5 nm) inside an electric-harbor-craft framework MPA already supports. (2) Singapore-radial Quanta-LR fan: Singapore ↔ Batam (~12 nm cross-border), Singapore ↔ Bintan (~25 nm), Singapore ↔ Tioman (~110 nm), Singapore ↔ Desaru (~25 nm). All routes in our spine. (3) Singapore-flagged registration as the certification anchor for Navier vessels operating across SEA — accelerates Grab regional rollout.

narrative.headline: Riau Islands — Singapore cross-border anchor
narrative.body: Steady-state. Batam, Bintan, Karimun: all sub-50 nm from Singapore — Pioneer II routes. Anambas/Natuna as Quanta-LR entry points. Singapore-flag + Indonesia bilateral water-mode framework is the MPA + IDN MoT joint workstream.

narrative.headline: Malaysia — cross-border to Desaru, Tioman, Mersing
narrative.body: Steady-state. Singapore ↔ Desaru, Singapore ↔ Tioman, Tioman ↔ Mersing (~55 nm corrected). MPA + Marine Department Malaysia bilateral on water-mode ridehail and tourism corridor regulation.

partner_view.value_prop: Singapore is Southeast Asia's most credible maritime regulatory home and a natural hub for next-generation passenger vessels. Hydrofoil electric and hybrid vessels offer a quiet, low-emission, high-throughput option for harbour and regional routes — and a certification pathway in MPA waters that sets the standard for the wider region.
partner_view.call_to_action: Open a certification and harbour-route trial pathway in MPA waters.

title: Navier × Maldives Resorts
subtitle: Silent, zero-wake island transfers — Velana arrivals to the atolls
executive_summary: Maldives luxury resorts compete on the quality of the guest journey, and today that journey depends on noisy speedboats and weather-limited seaplanes. Hydrofoil vessels offer a quieter, smoother, near-zero-wake transfer from Velana to the atolls that protects the reefs resorts are built around and elevates arrivals to match the rooms. The network can run electric for short hops and hybrid for the longer atoll runs, with no shore-charging dependency.

narrative.headline: Velana — the arrival backbone
narrative.body: Velana International is the single gateway for nearly every resort guest. A hydrofoil shuttle layer from the Velana seaplane and speedboat terminals connects directly to resort jetties across the atolls, smoothing the most friction-heavy part of the trip.

narrative.headline: Atoll resort jetties
narrative.body: Soneva, Six Senses, COMO, Taj, and Banyan Tree properties each operate private jetties that are natural boarding points for a quiet, reef-safe transfer mode. Longer atoll runs sit within hybrid range; shorter intra-atoll hops are all-electric.

partner_view.value_prop: A guest transfer as refined as the villa. Hydrofoil vessels deliver silent, smooth, near-zero-wake arrivals from Velana to the atolls, protecting the reefs and turning a logistics step into a signature moment — with a lower emissions profile guests increasingly expect.
partner_view.call_to_action: Pilot a Velana-to-atoll hydrofoil transfer on a flagship resort route.

title: Navier × Qatar Waterborne Transit
subtitle: Doha Bay and Corniche — quiet electric harbour mobility
executive_summary: Doha's bay and Corniche are an ideal setting for quiet, fast, low-wake waterborne transit linking the cultural, commercial, and waterfront districts. Hydrofoil electric vessels offer a clean, high-throughput option that reduces road load and emissions while giving the waterfront a modern, low-noise mobility layer.

narrative.headline: Corniche + Old Doha Port
narrative.body: Named public boarding points at the Doha Corniche ferry station and the Old Doha Port cruise terminal anchor a harbour route network. Calm-bay conditions suit a near-zero-wake hydrofoil well.

partner_view.value_prop: A clean, quiet, high-throughput waterborne transit option for Doha Bay. Hydrofoil electric vessels link waterfront districts with zero direct emissions and minimal wake and noise — easing road congestion and adding a modern mobility layer to the Corniche.
partner_view.call_to_action: Trial an all-electric harbour route between the Corniche and Old Doha Port.
